To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zinc-dependent low levels of thymulin are present in patients suffering from type 1 diabetes.

(1) the zinc-dependent thymic hormone is reduced in type I diabetes; (2) this reduction is not due to a thymus failure but to a zinc deficiency; and (3) the zinc-dependent failure of the thymic hormone might account for the insulin-independent immunological defects associated with type I (insu-lin-dependent) diabetes.
the serum level of the thymic hormone thymulin, which is biologically active when bound to zinc, is reduced in diabetic patients, whereas the level of inactive thymulin is increased.
